claims: Issue #596 reports s(365) <= 19.621320343560, s(370) <= 19.767730746255 and s(460) <= 21.959969683021, the exact rational sides of the certificates rounded up at 12 places, for the beyond-horizon list; it prints the certificate sides 19.621320343559642573398746289751, 19.767730746254604158720695152869 and 21.959969683020493134160191682454 with the SHA-256 of each search/packer/candidates/fresh_nNNN.cert.

The issue says all three are two-piece compositions, from a pass over the packings posted in issues 586 and 593: at 365 the register's s(199) (Nate Chaoweeraprasit, SQUISH) whole with Erich Friedman's s(26) whole, so S* = s(26) + 14 = 14 + 7/2 + 3/sqrt(2); at 370 Francisco Couzo's s(175) (issue 488) whole with a 38-square (h + 2) x h rectangle from the author's rectangle search; at 460 an 81-square crop of Nate Chaoweeraprasit's s(306) (issue 481) and a 130-square crop of Francisco Couzo's s(380) (issue 586).

Each side is an 80-digit KKT point with positive multipliers on the load-bearing contacts, a reduced Hessian positive semidefinite modulo exact flat motions and a first-order MILP that finds no descent; the issue calls these numerical evidence, not interval proofs, and claims no optimality.
